text: High availability and disaster recovery get lumped together constantly, but they answer different questions. HA survives a local failure with little or no downtime. DR survives a regional disaster, failing over to a different geography entirely.

Azure SQL Database's own service tiers show this split. General Purpose separates compute from remote storage — if the compute node fails, a new one reattaches to the same durable storage. That's HA for this tier: swap the compute, keep the storage.

Business Critical takes a different approach — a cluster of nodes, each with local storage, kept continuously in sync. Any replica can take over almost instantly if the primary fails. Different mechanism, same job: surviving a local failure.

Neither architecture, by itself, is disaster recovery. If the whole region goes down, both need a separate mechanism — geo-replication or failover groups — to fail over somewhere else. HA and DR are related, but genuinely different problems.
Keep that split in mind for the rest of this chapter. Next up: RPO and RTO, the business decisions that determine which of these tools you actually need.
